controls.title: Run the Docker daemon as a non-root user
controls.summary: The Docker daemon should run as a non-root user to reduce the attack surface of the host system in the event of a container escape.
implementationChecklist: Enable rootless mode for Docker daemon
Verify daemon runs under a non-privileged user account
Ensure cgroup and namespace isolation is properly configured
evidenceExamples: ps -ef | grep dockerd output showing non-root user

controls.title: Restrict network traffic between containers
controls.summary: By default, Docker allows unrestricted network traffic between containers on the same host. This should be restricted to reduce the attack surface.
implementationChecklist: Set --icc=false on the Docker daemon
Use custom bridge networks with explicit container linking
Implement network policies for container-to-container communication
evidenceExamples: docker network ls output showing custom networks

controls.title: Enable Content Trust for image verification
controls.summary: Docker Content Trust provides digital signatures for data sent to and received from remote Docker registries, ensuring image integrity and publisher identity.
implementationChecklist: Set DOCKER_CONTENT_TRUST=1 environment variable
Configure Notary server for private registries
Sign all images before pushing to registries
evidenceExamples: Environment variable DOCKER_CONTENT_TRUST=1 set in profiles

controls.title: Enable user namespace support
controls.summary: User namespace remapping provides additional isolation by mapping container root to a non-privileged host user, reducing the impact of container breakout.
implementationChecklist: Configure --userns-remap in daemon.json
Create subordinate UID/GID ranges for the remapped user
Verify containers run with remapped UIDs

controls.title: Set ownership and permissions on docker.service
controls.summary: The docker.service file controls the Docker daemon systemd configuration. It should be owned by root with restricted permissions to prevent unauthorized modification.
implementationChecklist: Set ownership to root:root on docker.service
Set permissions to 644 or more restrictive
Audit file access periodically

controls.title: Set ownership and permissions on daemon.json
controls.summary: The daemon.json file contains Docker daemon configuration parameters. Access should be restricted to prevent unauthorized changes to daemon behavior.
implementationChecklist: Set ownership to root:root on /etc/docker/daemon.json
Set permissions to 644 or more restrictive
Monitor file changes with integrity monitoring tools
evidenceExamples: AIDE or OSSEC change detection reports

controls.title: Create a user for the container
controls.summary: Containers should not run as root. Create a non-root user in the Dockerfile and switch to it using the USER directive to limit the impact of a container compromise.
implementationChecklist: Add USER directive in Dockerfile after installing packages
Create a dedicated application user with minimal privileges
Verify running containers do not use root (docker inspect)

controls.title: Use trusted base images
controls.summary: Only use trusted and verified base images from official or curated repositories. Scan base images for vulnerabilities before use.
implementationChecklist: Use Docker Official Images or verified publisher images
Pin base images to specific digests (not :latest)
Scan base images with vulnerability scanners before use
evidenceExamples: Dockerfile FROM directives referencing official images with digests
Image scan reports for base images

controls.title: Do not install unnecessary packages
controls.summary: Minimize the attack surface by not installing unnecessary packages in containers. Each additional package increases the potential for vulnerabilities.
implementationChecklist: Use --no-install-recommends for apt-get
Use multi-stage builds to separate build and runtime
Consider distroless or minimal base images

controls.title: Add HEALTHCHECK instruction
controls.summary: Include HEALTHCHECK in Dockerfiles to enable container health monitoring. This allows orchestrators to detect and replace unhealthy containers automatically.
implementationChecklist: Add HEALTHCHECK instruction with appropriate check command
Set reasonable interval, timeout, and retries
Monitor health status in orchestration platform
evidenceExamples: docker inspect showing health check configuration

controls.title: Use COPY instead of ADD
controls.summary: Prefer COPY over ADD in Dockerfiles. ADD has auto-extraction and remote URL features that can introduce security risks like arbitrary file inclusion.
implementationChecklist: Replace ADD with COPY for local file operations
Only use ADD when tar auto-extraction is specifically needed
Never use ADD with remote URLs
evidenceExamples: Dockerfile using COPY instead of ADD

controls.title: Do not store secrets in Dockerfiles
controls.summary: Secrets such as credentials, tokens, and keys should never be stored in Dockerfiles or image layers. Use build secrets, environment variables, or secret management tools.
implementationChecklist: Use Docker BuildKit secrets (--secret) for build-time secrets
Use runtime secret management (Vault, AWS Secrets Manager)
Scan images and Dockerfiles for embedded secrets

controls.title: Do not disable AppArmor profile
controls.summary: AppArmor provides mandatory access control for containers. Do not run containers with --security-opt apparmor=unconfined as it removes important security restrictions.
implementationChecklist: Ensure containers run with default or custom AppArmor profiles
Do not use apparmor=unconfined
Create custom profiles for applications requiring specific access
evidenceExamples: docker inspect showing AppArmor profile applied

controls.title: Do not disable SELinux
controls.summary: SELinux provides mandatory access control enforcement. Containers should not bypass SELinux using --security-opt label:disable.
implementationChecklist: Verify SELinux is enabled and enforcing on the host
Do not use label:disable security option
Apply appropriate SELinux labels to containers

controls.title: Do not run containers with privileged flag
controls.summary: Running a container with --privileged gives it full access to the host, including all devices and kernel capabilities. This defeats container isolation entirely.
implementationChecklist: Never use --privileged flag in production
Use specific --cap-add for required capabilities instead
Audit running containers for privileged mode
evidenceExamples: Container orchestration policies preventing privileged mode

controls.title: Do not map privileged ports within containers
controls.summary: Do not map container ports to host privileged ports (below 1024). Privileged ports require root and increase the attack surface.
implementationChecklist: Map container ports to non-privileged host ports (1024+)
Use reverse proxies for ports 80/443 instead of direct mapping
Audit port mappings in container configurations
evidenceExamples: docker port output showing non-privileged mappings

controls.title: Do not share the host network namespace
controls.summary: Using --net=host gives the container full access to the host network stack, bypassing network isolation. Containers should use their own network namespace.
implementationChecklist: Do not use --net=host in production containers
Use Docker bridge or overlay networks
Only use host networking for monitoring/infrastructure containers with documented justification
evidenceExamples: docker inspect showing NetworkMode is not host

controls.title: Limit memory usage for containers
controls.summary: Set memory limits on containers to prevent a single container from exhausting all host memory, which could cause denial of service to other containers and the host.
implementationChecklist: Set --memory flag on all production containers
Configure memory limits in orchestration manifests
Monitor container memory usage and set alerts
evidenceExamples: docker inspect showing Memory limits configured
Kubernetes resource limits in pod specs

controls.title: Set container CPU priority
controls.summary: Set CPU shares or limits on containers to prevent a single container from monopolizing host CPU resources.
implementationChecklist: Set --cpu-shares or --cpus flag on containers
Configure CPU limits in orchestration manifests
Monitor container CPU usage

controls.title: Mount container root filesystem as read-only
controls.summary: Mount the container root filesystem as read-only to prevent runtime modification of the container filesystem, reducing the impact of compromised containers.
implementationChecklist: Use --read-only flag when running containers
Use tmpfs mounts for directories requiring write access
Verify application works correctly with read-only root

controls.title: Do not share the host PID namespace
controls.summary: Using --pid=host gives the container visibility into all host processes. This breaks process isolation and can expose sensitive information.
implementationChecklist: Do not use --pid=host for application containers
Use separate PID namespaces (default behavior)
Document and justify any exceptions
evidenceExamples: docker inspect showing PidMode is not host

controls.title: Restrict container from acquiring additional privileges
controls.summary: Set --security-opt=no-new-privileges to prevent container processes from gaining additional privileges via setuid or setgid binaries.
implementationChecklist: Use --security-opt=no-new-privileges on all containers
Configure in orchestration security contexts
Audit running containers for this setting
evidenceExamples: docker inspect showing no-new-privileges security option

controls.title: Use PIDs cgroup limit
controls.summary: Limit the number of processes a container can create using the --pids-limit flag to prevent fork bomb attacks.
implementationChecklist: Set --pids-limit to a reasonable value for each container
Monitor process counts inside containers
Set alerts for containers approaching PID limits

controls.title: Do not mount the Docker socket inside containers
controls.summary: Mounting /var/run/docker.sock inside a container gives it full control over the Docker daemon, equivalent to root access on the host.
implementationChecklist: Never mount docker.sock in production containers
Use Docker API over TLS with client certificates if remote access needed
Audit volume mounts for docker.sock references
evidenceExamples: docker inspect showing no docker.sock mount
